headline: DMV hoops belongs to the court, the county and the high school.
summary: DC basketball lives outside the arena. The Goodman League at Barry Farm is the city's Rucker, the talent runs through the WCAC and Prince George's County, and Ward 8 is the Wizards' own grassroots base. Nike's way in is DMV-only product made with the Goodman, the high schools and the women's game. Under Armour dresses Maryland, though, and Trae Young, just re-signed, wears adidas.

insights.title: Barry Farm is DC's Rucker
insights.detail: The Goodman League has played outdoors for decades at the Barry Farm Recreation Center in Ward 8. The neighborhood was founded after the Civil War for freed Black families, and locals still call it "Barry Farms". The league peaked in the 2011 lockout, when Kevin Durant and the Wizards' John Wall played there. A Goodman all-star team also beat LA's Drew League by one point in DC.
insights.implication: Don't invent a Nike league. License and fund the Goodman, with its organizers controlling the marks. Make its June-August season the summer anchor for the Dybantsa-era Wizards.

insights.title: Locals claim pros by school and county
insights.detail: PG County claims Durant (Seat Pleasant), DeMatha's Victor Oladipo, Markelle Fultz and Jerami Grant, and Northwestern High's Jeff Green. DC proper claims Spingarn's Elgin Baylor and Dave Bing and Carroll's John Thompson. Montgomery County claims Sidwell Friends' Josh Hart. Northern Virginia claims Reston's Grant Hill.
insights.implication: Make the high school, county and area code the unit of the story, not a generic "DMV" label. License the school marks, and name the gym in each athlete's story.

insights.title: The WCAC is the rivalry engine
insights.detail: The Washington Catholic Athletic Conference (DeMatha, Gonzaga, Archbishop Carroll, St. John's, Bishop McNamara, Paul VI, O'Connell) is widely called the toughest high school league in the country. DeMatha's 46-43 win over Lew Alcindor's Power Memorial at Cole Field House in 1965 made Morgan Wootten's program a national name. Each March, DC's public-school Interhigh meets the private powers in the DC State Athletic Association tournament.
insights.implication: Time school-pride drops to the late-February WCAC final and the March state tournament. Fund Interhigh gyms and uniforms so Nike isn't only dressing the tuition schools.

insights.title: Three brands fight for one region
insights.detail: Under Armour is headquartered in Baltimore and dresses the Maryland Terrapins. Arlington's Azzi Fudd, the St. John's alum who was 2025 Final Four Most Outstanding Player for UConn, has had an Under Armour NIL deal. Trae Young, just re-signed for four years, has an adidas signature shoe. Nike's local assets are Durant's long-term deal, Team Takeover on the Nike EYBL circuit and Jordan Brand's Kiki Rice.
insights.implication: Lead DMV product with the team, the Goodman and the schools, not Young's personal marks. Lock in Nike's DMV athletes and Takeover alumni before rivals do.

insights.title: Ward 8 is the franchise's grassroots base
insights.detail: CareFirst Arena on the St. Elizabeths East campus in Congress Heights is home to the Mystics, the Capital City Go-Go and the Wizards' practice facility. It's a short drive from Barry Farm. The Go-Go are named for DC's own music, which the city made its official music in 2020 after the 2019 #DontMuteDC protests.
insights.implication: Treat east of the Anacostia as one corridor. Go-Go games, Mystics nights and Goodman runs can share a Ward 8 product line, made with go-go musicians and Ward 8 organizers who are paid and credited.

insights.title: Women's hoops is a title-winning second engine
insights.detail: The Mystics won the 2019 WNBA title with Elena Delle Donne and drafted Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen at No. 3 and No. 4 in 2025. DC prep schools produced Fudd (St. John's) and Kiki Rice (Sidwell Friends), a Jordan Brand NIL athlete. Nike makes every WNBA uniform.
insights.implication: Design DC hoops product women's-first, and keep it selling May-September when the Wizards are dark. Use the Mystics and Rice as the Nike-side faces, and leave Fudd out.

insights.title: DC wore Georgetown before it wore the Wizards
insights.detail: John Thompson's 1980s "Hoya Paranoia" teams put Georgetown Starter-style jackets and gray hoodies on DC streets and in hip-hop. Allen Iverson's mid-1990s kente-trimmed uniform is still a top throwback. The Hoyas still share Capital One Arena with the Wizards.
insights.implication: The appetite for heritage outerwear is real, but the marks are licensed IP. Borrow the silhouettes (satin bench jackets, heavyweight gray fleece) for Wizards and DMV product, not Hoyas graphics.

places.name: Barry Farm Recreation Center
places.why: Home court of the Goodman League, and the outdoor run every DC hooper and visiting pro is measured against.

places.name: CareFirst Arena
places.why: The 4,200-seat building east of the river that holds the Mystics, the Capital City Go-Go and the Wizards' practice gym.

places.name: Seat Pleasant Activity Center
places.why: The gym where Kevin Durant learned the game, and a pilgrimage point for PG County hoopers.

places.name: DeMatha Catholic High School
places.why: Morgan Wootten's program and the WCAC's most decorated pro factory: Adrian Dantley, Oladipo, Fultz and Jerami Grant.

places.name: Cole Field House
places.kind: historic arena, now a Maryland training complex
places.why: Site of DeMatha's 1965 upset of Power Memorial and Texas Western's 1966 NCAA title with five Black starters.

places.name: Xfinity Center
places.why: Maryland's home court and Under Armour's flagship college stage in the DMV. Maryland Madness tips off here each October.

places.name: Burr Gymnasium
places.why: Home of the Howard Bison and DC's HBCU basketball pride.

people.name: Kevin Durant
people.role: DC-born, Seat Pleasant-raised NBA star, long-term Nike signature athlete and co-founder of Boardroom
people.why: The DMV's biggest hooper. He wears 35 for his late youth coach and ran at Barry Farm in 2011, so any KD-DMV product has to start with him and his team.

people.name: John Thompson Jr.
people.role: Georgetown coach 1972-99, DC native and Archbishop Carroll alum (died 2020)
people.why: The first Black coach to win an NCAA title (1984) and the author of Hoya Paranoia. DC treats him as its basketball patriarch.

people.name: Morgan Wootten
people.why: He built the national model for high school programs, and his 1965 upset of Power Memorial is DMV basketball scripture.

people.name: Elgin Baylor and Dave Bing
people.role: Hall of Famers from DC's Spingarn High
people.why: DC's original NBA greats. Their story lives in Interhigh memory and old-head debates.

people.name: Kiki Rice
people.role: Guard from DC, Sidwell Friends and UCLA; Jordan Brand NIL athlete
people.why: Her Jordan Brand NIL deal gives Nike a DC-born face for women's product.

people.name: Team Takeover
people.role: DMV travel program on the Nike EYBL circuit
people.why: The region's flagship Nike grassroots program, and the most direct line to the next DMV pros.

people.name: Goodman League
people.role: Summer pro-am at Barry Farm, Ward 8
people.why: DC's most storied outdoor league, where NBA players have proven themselves at home.

people.name: Gilbert Arenas
people.role: Former Wizards star; host of the Gil's Arena podcast
people.why: Agent Zero is still the Wizards' cult hero, and his show is one of hoops' biggest. But his 2009-10 locker-room gun incident and a 2025 federal illegal-gambling charge (outcome to confirm) mean any tie-in needs care.

moments.name: Goodman League summer season
moments.why: DC's marquee outdoor run, and the best window for Wizards player appearances, summer product and Ward 8 youth clinics.

moments.name: Maryland Madness and Hoya Madness
moments.why: College tip-off events at Xfinity Center and Georgetown open DMV hoops season alongside Wizards camp.

moments.name: Emirates NBA Cup home opener: Hornets at Wizards
moments.why: The Dybantsa era's first Cup Night at home. Bring Goodman, Interhigh and WCAC teams in, and launch DMV product.

moments.name: Capital City Go-Go season
moments.why: Affordable pro hoops in Ward 8, and a recurring stage for go-go-themed product.

moments.name: WCAC tournament final
moments.why: The DMV's biggest high school night, when the DeMatha, Gonzaga, Paul VI, St. John's and Carroll fan bases peak.

moments.name: DCSAA state championships
moments.why: DC's public Interhigh schools meet the private and charter powers for a city title.

moments.name: Washington Mystics season
moments.why: Keeps DC hoops product selling through the Wizards' offseason.

vocabulary.meaning: DC, Maryland and Virginia. Its players insist "DMV hoops" is the best high school basketball in the country.
DC's all-purpose "bro" or "man": "Run it back, moe."
DC's all-purpose noun for a thing, place, song or game: "That jont was crazy."
Someone corny or out of place. On court, the player whose game or gear doesn't fit.
Acting crazy or not paying attention, as in a wild shot or a blown defensive assignment.
Shorthand for the Goodman League, played at what locals call "Barry Farms".
The go-go practice of shouting out neighborhoods and crews from the stage. DMV hoop pride works the same way, by block, ward and county.
Prince George's County, Maryland, the majority-Black suburb that claims Durant, Oladipo, Fultz and Jerami Grant.

designCues.cue: Area-code roll call: 202, 301/240 and 703/571 as jersey numerals, or across the back yoke of shooting shirts, in a heavy block sports font.
designCues.source: DMV hoopers identify by area code and county, the way go-go bands shout out neighborhoods in the roll call.
designCues.use: Use numbers and county names only, never crew names, and vet each with local organizers.

designCues.cue: Go-go flyer dayglo: fluorescent yellow with hot orange #FF6B1A and pink #FF3FA4 accents, behind stacked black wood-type lettering.
designCues.source: The neon block-letter posters that advertised go-go shows across DC for decades, printed by Baltimore's Globe Poster.
designCues.use: Use it for summer-league and Go-Go night graphics. Commission DC poster artists and credit the Globe tradition, rather than copying archive posters.

designCues.cue: Wizards red #E31837 on navy #002B5C with silver #C4CED4 trim, as the base for pro-am kits.
designCues.source: The Wizards' team palette, the shared language of DC's pro teams.
designCues.use: Use it so a Barry Farm jersey reads as the home team. Add Goodman marks only under license.

designCues.cue: Three stars, two bars: the DC flag's red stars and bars as waistband taping, or a break inside a numeral.
designCues.source: George Washington's family coat of arms, now the DC flag locals tattoo and print on everything.
designCues.use: It's a civic symbol, not team IP. Keep its proportions intact so it reads as the District, not decoration.

designCues.cue: 35 for Seat Pleasant: Durant's number as a memorial numeral with a Seat Pleasant wordmark.
designCues.source: Durant wears 35 for his youth coach from the Seat Pleasant rec center, who was killed at 35 in 2005.
designCues.use: Only with Durant's involvement and blessing. It's a memorial, not a graphic.

designCues.cue: 46-43 at Cole Field House: a hidden scoreline print or hangtag story.
designCues.source: DeMatha's 1965 upset of Lew Alcindor's Power Memorial and Texas Western's 1966 title, both played at Maryland's Cole Field House.
designCues.use: For school-heritage product, licensed with DeMatha and told in the school's own words.

designCues.cue: Cherry-blossom pink as a lead color, with navy as the supporting tone.
designCues.source: The Tidal Basin blossoms behind the 2022-23 City Edition the Wizards are reported to be reviving for 2026-27.
designCues.use: Tie grassroots product to the City Edition. Match the exact uniform palette once it's confirmed.

designCues.cue: Satin bench jacket and heavyweight gray fleece.
designCues.source: Georgetown's 1980s Hoya Paranoia era, when Starter-style jackets and gray hoodies were DC's street uniform.
designCues.use: Use the silhouettes for Wizards and DMV outerwear. Never use Hoyas marks without a license.

productHooks: Goodman League summer kit: licensed reversible jerseys, warm-up tees and ref shirts in Wizards red and navy, dropped in June at Barry Farm. Licensing fees and a share of sales go to the league and Barry Farm youth programs.

DMV Area Code pack: 202, 301/240 and 703/571 shooting shirts, shorts and socks, women's cut first. Sell it through DMV doors and Nike digital, with stories naming each area code's pros and high schools.

"Claimed" school-heritage warm-ups: licensed collabs with DeMatha, Archbishop Carroll and Northwestern, plus an Interhigh tribute to Spingarn's Baylor and Bing. Release them for the WCAC final and March state tournament, and fund Interhigh gyms and uniforms.

Ward 8 women's hoops capsule with the Mystics, using Nike's WNBA uniform partnership and Kiki Rice if her deal allows. Launch it at the May home opener at CareFirst Arena and sell it through September.
KD Seat Pleasant colorway and court refurbishment at the Seat Pleasant Activity Center, built with Durant and his team and unveiled with a free youth clinic.
watchouts: Brand conflicts: Trae Young is an adidas signature athlete, and Baltimore's Under Armour dresses Maryland. Keep Nike DMV product led by the team, leagues and schools. Confirm Dybantsa's and Davis's deals before building player stories.

The franchise dropped "Bullets" in 1997 over gun violence, and the Barry Farm and Congress Heights courts sit in the wards hit hardest. Keep Bullets nostalgia and gun wordplay out of community and Ward 8 product.
Go-go roll calls name neighborhood crews, and some crew names carry long-running beefs. Use wards, area codes and rec-center names vetted with local organizers, never crew names.

Barry Farm's public-housing redevelopment displaced longtime residents. Goodman projects need the league's organizers and former residents at the table, paid licensing for league marks and money that stays in Ward 8.

Georgetown, Maryland, Howard and high school marks need licensing. Georgetown's 1990s kente trim borrows a Ghanaian textile, so commission Ghanaian weavers rather than printing faux kente. Treat Globe Poster's archive as someone else's IP.
